series_key: integrate your own llm into ea
mechanism: Fine-tune GPT-2 on space-joined FX close strings (60 closes/line from llm_data.csv). At inference, prompt with latest 20 closes, generate next ~40 closes; let A=mean(last 20), B=mean(predicted 40); buy if B>A, sell if B<A, flat if nearly equal. Causal LM treated as multi-step close path sensor.
data_needed: llm_data.csv / train.txt of 5M closes; GPT-2 tokenizer+LMHead; Trainer full fine-tune; MSE/RMSE/NRMSE test harness
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Unnamed FX currency pair; PERIOD 5M; windows 20 in / 40 out (60-token blocks)
why_new_for_mis: Treats a causal LLM as an explicit multi-step FX close path sensor whose mean-path tilt becomes a directional regime read—distinct from classifier or classical AR sensors.
quote: If the average value B of 40 predicted values is greater than the average value A of the current latest 20 closing prices, then buy.

series_key: integrate your own llm into ea
mechanism: After GPT-2 generates future closes, compute MSE then RMSE and NRMSE=RMSE/(max(true)-min(generated)). Shows tiny absolute MSE/RMSE on ~0.61 FX prices can hide large relative error (NRMSE≈0.585 ≈58.5% of observed range)—a sensing-quality gate for sequence predictors on small-tick FX.
data_needed: Aligned true vs generated close lists; sklearn MSE; numpy max/min range
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same FX pair 5M close series as fine-tune dataset
why_new_for_mis: NRMSE-vs-price-range as a mandatory relative accuracy sensor for FX LLM forecasts prevents MIS from trusting misleading near-zero MSE on pip-scale prices.
quote: the NRMSE value is 0.5850514133390986, which means that the prediction error accounts for about 58.5% of the range of observed values.

series_key: integrate your own llm into ea
mechanism: Same 20→40 close-completion task as full fine-tune, but freezes GPT-2 and trains LoRA adapters via peft LoraConfig(lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.1); load with PeftModel.from_pretrained for inference. Compares train time/VRAM/NRMSE vs full FT—LoRA is cheaper but NRMSE more run-to-run unstable under do_sample.
data_needed: train.txt; peft LoraConfig/get_peft_model/PeftModel; GPT-2 base; same prompt of last 20 closes
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same FX 5M close dataset as Part 5-I
why_new_for_mis: Parameter-efficient LoRA adapters as the FX close-path sensor give MIS a lower-VRAM neural channel with explicit stability trade-offs vs full FT.
quote: From an efficiency standpoint, it is clear that LoRA-tuning is superior in terms of training speed, inference speed, and memory usage compared to full-parameter fine-tuning.

Horizontal compare vs full FT and LoRA on MSE/RMSE/NRMSE and VRAM.
data_needed: Adapter/GPT2LMHeadModelWithAdapters classes; train.txt block_size=60; Trainer 3 epochs

series_key: integrate your own llm into ea
mechanism: Python socket server loads Adapter-tuned GPT-2; EA timer (60s) CopyClose of data_len=100 bars and sends CSV prices; server takes last encoder_length=20, generates prediction_length=10 closes, compares last_price to mean(predicted): sell if last≥mean else buy. EA holds single position flipping on signal. Backtested on NZDUSD.
data_needed: gpt2_Adapter-tuning weights; tokenizer; socket host/port; CopyClose buffer; mean of generated floats
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NZDUSD (model trained on NZDUSD); EA timer 60s / chart period 0 (current); encoder 20 / pred 10
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes the FX close-path LLM as a live last-vs-forecast-mean directional sensor over sockets—MIS can ingest the buy/sell stream as a neural regime channel.
quote: If the difference surpasses 0, send a "buy" signal; if less than 0, send a "sell" signal; if equal to 0, do not send any signal.

series_key: integrating mql5 with data processing packages
mechanism: ExtractFeatures builds a 12-dim vector for MLP expected-reward regression: ATR-normalized distance to last swing high/low, swingStrength=(high-low)/ATR, swingDir ±1, raw ATR, RSI/100, momentum/ATR, linreg slope/ATR over InpTrendLookback, volume ratio, breakAbove/breakBelow flags, time-of-day hour/24. Posted to Flask /predict.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart _Symbol/_Period (Dynamic Swing Architecture EA); ATR/RSI 14, Mom 10, Trend/Vol lookback 20 defaults
why_new_for_mis: Compact ATR-scaled multi-aspect snapshot (structure+vol+momentum+volume+TOD) is a reusable MIS feature schema for online neural reward sensing.
quote: The ExtractFeatures function creates a comprehensive 12-dimensional market snapshot by transforming raw price data into normalized, ATR-scaled features that capture multiple aspects of market behavior, including volatility (ATR), momentum (RSI and price momentum), swing dynamics

series_key: integrating mql5 with data processing packages
mechanism: After each trade, EA POSTs features+action+entry/exit+pips+reward to /feedback; server appends to feedback_buffer and CSV; background trainer_loop retrains MLP (Adam+MSE, 40 epochs) when buffer≥RETRAIN_THRESHOLD (100), refits StandardScaler, exports live_model.onnx for continued inference—closed-loop adaptation to live outcomes.
data_needed: feedback_buffer dicts; reward from CalculateReward(profit,pips,volume); Flask /feedback;/retrain; ONNX export
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Live MT5 symbol/tf carried in feedback payload; Python server 127.0.0.1:5000
why_new_for_mis: Outcome-conditioned online retrain loop turns MIS from a static model consumer into a self-updating neural sensor driven by realized trade reward.
quote: Periodically, the model uses this data to retrain or adjust its weights, producing a more accurate and responsive version that is later re-exported to ONNX for MQL5 inference.
